newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish longer yields edge down, crown weakens.
newsitem.headline: Swedish longer yields edge down, crown weakens.

text.p: Swedish debt yields closed virtually unchanged from Monday's levels in quiet trade.
"We've more or less tracked foreign markets even though we've decreased the spread to Germany," one dealer said.
Yields began the day slightly higher in line with Monday's weaker U.S. market, but fell back as debt markets firmed.
The Riksbank's 15 basis point repo rate cut to 5.25 percent was fully discounted in the market, and neither than nor strong Swedish macro-indicators managed to spark any reaction in the market.

Sweden's July producer price index fell by 0.1 percent, resulting in a record low year on year figure of -4.3 percent. The index has fallen consistently since it peaked at 11.5 year on year in May 1995.

Sweden's trade balance for July showed a surplus of 9.5 billion crowns, just under market expectations of a 9.7 billion crown surplus. At the same time, the record high June figure was revised upwards from 14.3 billion to 15.0 billion crowns.
